title: Air India and Drukair Partner to Boost India-Bhutan Travel With Single-Ticket Bookings
excerpt: The new interline agreement enables seamless connections between Air India's global network and Drukair's Bhutan routes, with coordinated baggage transfers through Delhi.
body:
• Air India and Drukair, Royal Bhutan Airlines, have signed an interline agreement enabling single-ticket bookings across both carriers' networks with coordinated baggage transfers.
  • Air India passengers can now connect seamlessly to Bhutan's Paro via Delhi, with onward Drukair flights to Bumthang, Gelephu, and Yonphula.
  • Drukair passengers gain access to Air India's domestic network via Delhi, Guwahati, and Kolkata, plus international routes to London, New York, San Francisco, Sydney, Toronto, and Vancouver.
  • The partnership gives Air India connectivity to nearly all SAARC countries through its own or partner networks.

Air India and Drukair, Royal Bhutan Airlines, announced an interline partnership on August 26 that enables passengers to book single-ticket itineraries combining flights on both carriers, with coordinated baggage transfers through Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport.

The agreement significantly expands travel options between India, Bhutan, and international destinations, eliminating the need for passengers to recheck luggage during transit.

What the Partnership Covers

Under the interline arrangement, Air India passengers can travel to Bhutan's Paro airport via Delhi from across the airline's expanding international network. From Paro, travellers can connect onward via Drukair to domestic Bhutanese destinations including Bumthang, Gelephu, and Yonphula.

Drukair passengers, in turn, gain access to Air India's domestic network through Delhi, Guwahati, and Kolkata, with onward connections to major Indian cities such as Bengaluru, Mumbai, and Kochi. The partnership also unlocks Air India's long-haul international routes, covering destinations including London Heathrow, New York JFK, Newark, Paris Charles de Gaulle, Frankfurt, San Francisco, Melbourne, Sydney, Toronto Pearson, Vancouver, and Colombo.

Passengers will benefit from competitive interline fares, improved routing options, and greater flexibility when planning journeys across the two airlines' combined networks, according to Air India.

"Our partnership with Drukair reinforces our commitment to strengthening connectivity across the SAARC region, which we consider our extended home market. Bhutan is a valued part of this region, and we are happy to enable easy access to Bhutan for our guests."

— Nipun Aggarwal, Chief Commercial Officer, Air India

Strengthening SAARC Connectivity

The Tata Group-owned Air India said the partnership gives it connectivity to nearly all countries in the SAARC region through its own or partner network, with Bhutan now added to its wider regional offering. The airline has been steadily expanding its interline and codeshare partnerships as part of its ongoing transformation under Tata ownership.

Drukair CEO Tandi Wangchuk called the agreement "a significant milestone" for the Bhutanese national carrier. "Through this interline partnership with Air India, our customers will benefit from seamless journeys, expanded access to key international markets, and improved connectivity across India and beyond," Wangchuk said.

New Options for Indian and NRI Travellers

Bhutan has become an increasingly popular destination for Indian travellers, drawn by its Buddhist monasteries, Himalayan landscapes, and reputation as one of the world's most sustainable tourism destinations. The country reopened to international tourists in September 2022 after a pandemic-era closure, introducing a daily Sustainable Development Fee for visitors — though Indian nationals are exempt from the fee.

For NRIs based in cities served by Air India's long-haul network — including San Francisco, New York, London, Toronto, and Vancouver — the interline agreement creates one-ticket routing to Paro that was previously unavailable without separate bookings. The coordinated baggage handling through Delhi is a practical improvement that removes a common friction point for international travellers connecting to Bhutan.

What's Next

The partnership is expected to support both tourism and business travel between India and Bhutan by lowering booking complexity and offering competitive fares. Air India continues to expand its partner network as part of its fleet and route expansion under Tata Group, with additional interline and codeshare agreements likely as the airline grows its international footprint.
